summary:
Sabrina Carpenter’s “Espresso,” released April 11, 2024, was the lead single from her sixth album, *Short n’ Sweet*. Carpenter wrote it with Amy Allen and Steph Jones; Julian Bunetta produced it. Recorded in France, California, and Tennessee, the song blends pop, funk, and dance styles, with lyrics about confidence and femininity. Its guitar and drum loops came from Oliver’s “Power Tools Sample Pack III.” Carpenter said she wrote it quickly in Chailland, France, in 2023; while her team supported the song, label executives initially questioned releasing it as a single.

Critics praised its catchy hook, playful lyrics, and groove. “That’s that me espresso” became a meme and prompted debate over its grammar. *Pitchfork* ranked it No. 30 on its 2024 list of the 100 best songs of the 2020s so far, and Nine Inch Nails’ Trent Reznor named it his top song of 2024.

The song reached No. 3 on the US *Billboard* Hot 100, where it charted for 65 weeks, and No. 1 on the *Billboard* Global 200. It topped charts in more than 20 countries, including the UK, Australia, Ireland, and Belgium, and reached the top 10 in at least 20 more. It earned Platinum or higher certification in 14 countries, including Diamond in Australia and France, and has more than 3.2 billion Spotify streams.

Dave Meyers directed the music video, released April 12, 2024. Set at a lake, it follows Carpenter and friends through a playful beachside escapade involving a speedboat, a stolen wallet, and a police arrest; it ends with music from her next single, “Please Please Please.”

Carpenter debuted the song live at Coachella in April 2024. Other performances included *Saturday Night Live*, BBC Radio 1’s Big Weekend, the MTV Video Music Awards, and the Grammys. She performed it as the encore on the *Short n’ Sweet Tour*, joined Taylor Swift for a mashup during Swift’s 2024 Eras Tour, and performed it at Coachella and the Met Gala in 2026. It won the 2024 VMA for Song of the Year—Carpenter’s first VMA—and two Grammys: Best Pop Solo Performance and Best Remixed Recording. It was also nominated for Record of the Year.

The song featured in *Just Dance 2025 Edition* and Fortnite, the film *The Bad Guys 2*, a Japanese TV drama, *Law & Order: SVU*, and *Emily in Paris*. Ariana Grande parodied it on *SNL*; Carpenter praised the performance, and the sketch gained more than 80 million TikTok views. Carpenter also inspired an Absolut–Kahlúa espresso martini kit and a Dunkin’ brown-sugar shaken espresso drink.
